observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a cigarette lying horizontally on a dark granular surface against a black background. From left to right: a tan/cork filter, a band of white paper, a glowing red ember at the burn line, and a column of grey ash. The filter's left end stays fixed at the frame's left edge throughout, so the cigarette and camera are stationary.
visible_changes: For the first ~0.9 s (frames 1-23) the ash forms a long column that extends all the way to the right edge of the frame.

Between t=0.88 s and t=0.92 s the long ash column breaks off; from frame 24 onward only a short ash stub with a pointed tip remains near the ember, and a few small ash fragments are visible on the surface below.
The red ember at the paper/ash junction glows and dims intermittently (notably brighter around frames 16, 29-32).
Thin wisps of smoke rise sporadically above the ember (e.g. frames 5, 9, 16, 19, 25, 36, 40).

The burn line drifts slightly leftward over the clip (the white-paper/ash boundary moves from roughly x=430 to x=375), indicating slow consumption of the tobacco while the filter position is unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the ash breaking off (vibration, air current, or natural collapse) is not visible.
What happens to the cigarette after this segment, and the portion of the cigarette left of the filter, are outside the crop.
uncertain_details: The exact instant of the ash break is bounded only by the 0.88 s and 0.92 s samples.
Whether each faint smoke wisp originates at the ember or drifts from off-frame is hard to confirm.
